findings.source_passage: a sort of eating of his own gums like a chimney hag
findings.why_it_matters: This grotesque simile is one of the most distinctive imagistic flares in the chapter — 'eating of his own gums like a chimney hag' is stylistically singular Melville and contributes to the uncanny texture of the dream figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'a sort of eating of his own gums like a chimney hag' after the merman's repeated muttering of 'wise Stubb, wise Stubb.'

findings.source_passage: Didn't he kick with right good will? it wasn't a common pitch pine leg he kicked with, was it?
findings.source_locator: paragraph 1, merman's speech arguing the insult
findings.why_it_matters: The merman's rhetorical logic — distinguishing the ivory leg from 'a common pitch pine leg' — is part of the chapter's thematic argument about honor and rank; flattening it removes interpretive texture about Ahab's exceptional status.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the merman's line: 'Didn't he kick with right good will? it wasn't a common pitch pine leg he kicked with, was it?'

findings.source_passage: I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!
findings.source_locator: end of paragraph 1, after the merman swims off
findings.why_it_matters: Stubb's three-beat comic rhythm — 'I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!' — is a signature voice moment; replacing it with 'Stubb woke in his hammock' entirely erases the comic cadence and first-person register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!'

findings.source_passage: "I don't know; it seems a sort of foolish to me, tho.'"
findings.source_locator: Flask's reply, after Stubb's dream narration
findings.why_it_matters: Flask's halting, bathetic non-answer — with its grammatically off 'a sort of foolish' — characterizes his flatness as a foil; reducing it to a single word 'Foolish' loses the characterizing awkwardness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Flask's line closer to verbatim: 'I don't know; it seems a sort of foolish to me, tho.'

findings.source_passage: in some queer fashion, to swim off into the air
findings.source_locator: end of merman episode, before Stubb wakes
findings.why_it_matters: The hedging 'somehow, in some queer fashion' preserves the dreamlike indeterminacy of the vision; the draft's 'seemed to swim off into the air' trims the qualifying hesitation that marks the narrator's (and Stubb's) uncertainty.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'all of a sudden seemed somehow, in some queer fashion, to swim off into the air.'

summary: No high-severity losses; two medium findings (the 'chimney hag' simile and 'pitch pine leg' distinction are absent, and 'I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!' is flattened) represent real voice degradation but fall below the regeneration threshold.
